threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a 10-minute walk is 'far'—everyone else’s already popped into five cafes before you reach the station.
Caught a ride on the 47 last night; a guy was singing old Bob Marley songs—everyone joined in. Never thought Brixton’s night buses had a karaoke vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw the guy across the street using a skateboard to haul his groceries. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can start your night with a currywurst at 3 AM from a street vendor and end it with fresh bread from a 24-hour bakery just down the block.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the difference between a taco truck on 24th and one just parked at the BART. It's all about the sauce.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 19 this morning, and a guy serenaded us with a ukulele. He claimed he was waiting for the 'real Muni experience.' Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all drink vermut on Sundays, but most locals avoid the crowds and head to quieter corner bars instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their obsession with the wrong paella recipe; they always think it’s served with chicken and chorizo, bless their hearts.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still flinch when you see an 'Expected Wait Time' sign at the bus stop, thinking it’s a cruel joke.
Caught a 59 last week, a bloke was trying to sell his mix tape to the driver. The driver just shook his head, but the mixtape was fire!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the kebab shop started recognizing my order and the owner asks about my weekend plans. That's when I felt truly at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: There's a hidden taco truck in Görlitzer Park that only shows up after 10 PM. It's like a secret club where the late-night crowds gather for late-night bites.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they subtly dodge the dog on the tracks at Civic Center while still sipping their Blue Bottle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus the other day where the driver paused to rescue a pigeon caught in the door. Only in SF would public transit become a rescue mission.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume all the best tapas spots are on the main square, but the hidden gems are just down the side streets where the locals gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their meticulous effort to order in perfect Catalan at local cafes, while locals already know it's just 'un cafè, si us plau.'
